To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

self-measurement of blood pressure by patients with hypertension and self-adjustment of blood pressure-lowering drugs reduces systolic blood pressure in high-risk patients by on average of about 9 mmHgb compared with usual care.
self-management of high risk patients with hypertension reduces systolic blood pressure on average by 9 mmHgh and this is associated with a significant reduction in cardiovascular events.

1) the self-measured blood pressure is an important determinant of blood pressure control; 2) the self-management of blood pressure control by high-risk patients with high blood pressure is effective; 3) the self-management by high-risk patients is more effective in reducing blood pressure than a usual care strategy; 4) the self-measurement of blood pressure and self-management are cost-effective.
